surface: CROWN JEWEL (combined surfaces): TOCTOU / races / detached-reattach / decision-future / second-order echo / import value-oracle / mapping-after-rename
summary_verdict: NO crown-jewel finding. No flag obtained, no value of any secret surfaced, no approval forged/bypassed, no unapproved preset/import/config/vault change, no cross-user break. Every value-bearing and state-changing primitive is console-gated; with no console attached the request.decision future can only ever become 'withdrawn', so the subtle/combined/race/TOCTOU angles the brief raised are all unreachable. Confirmed both by static caller analysis and live probes as redteam.
negative_results: DECISION FUTURE cannot become 'approved' from the socket (the master gate). Static: broker.approve/deny are called ONLY from server/console/app.py (<- request_card.py, passphrase-gated keyboard); state.decide is called ONLY from broker.approve(approved=True)/deny(approved=False); state.withdraw/set_result sets ONLY outcome='withdrawn'. request.decision is NEVER cancelled or set_exception'd by anyone (only the OUTER asyncio.shield wrapper is cancelled in _wait_decision via decision.cancel(), which leaves request.decision pending). So from a socket client the future resolves ONLY to 'withdrawn'. Live-confirmed: op_run (direct / via flag-preset / empty session) all return only {pending:true}; holding the connection open never yields a 2nd reply (TIMEOUT). No approver => no 'approved'.

_start_run (the ONLY caller of env_for, the ONLY value-bearing reply) is unreachable without a console. It is called at control.py:207 (session path, requires broker.resolve_run_in_session -> owned_session, i.e. an EXISTING live session owned by the caller) and control.py:218 (run path, only after `request.decision.result().outcome == 'approved'`). state.sessions is inserted into ONLY by create_session (state.py:188), called ONLY by broker.approve (broker.py:373). With no console, state.sessions stays empty forever (live-confirmed: `list` and `status` show LIVE SESSIONS (none) throughout). So neither _start_run path can be reached; env_for is never called with any mapping a socket client controls.

DETACHED-REATTACH does NOT create an approval window. op_session_start detach -> mark_detached (abandon_at = now+10min); a same-uid op_session_wait(request_id) resets abandon_at=None and re-attends, but _attend only waits on the (never-approved) decision and on the second disconnect re-arms mark_detached. Live: A session_start (req 25) dropped -> detached; B session_wait reset abandon_at and attended -> still {pending:true}, second read TIMEOUT. The reattach never resolves the decision, never starts a run, never surfaces a value. (It can keep a request pending with abandon_at briefly None, but that is the w1-session-1 slot-DoS, per-uid only, already recorded.)

TOCTOU in merged_for_approval / confirm_import_resolution / refresh_import is DEAD CODE for a socket attacker: all three are invoked ONLY inside broker.approve() (import branch) or broker._follow_rename_in_waiting_requests (called only from rename_secret, console-only). With no approve() ever called, the 'recompute vs stale, re-_show on change, type the passphrase again' logic never runs. Even if it did, _show has no listeners here (console attaches the only listener via broker.request_listeners.append), and it never returns anything to the socket client; it only re-renders the console card and raises RequestError back INTO approve().

MAPPING-AFTER-RENAME is not client-controllable. op_run uses request.mapping; mapping is mutated only by state.rename_secret (state.py:191), called only from broker.rename_secret, which is reachable only from the console /keys flow (check_rename + passphrase). No socket op renames a secret. A client picks its OWN mapping at request time via --with/--preset, but that is exactly what would be shown to (a nonexistent) approver; it changes nothing that env_for returns for an UNapproved request, and no run starts.

SECOND-ORDER VALUE ECHO is structurally absent. The flag/secret VALUE lives only in vault memory and in env_for() output. Traced every socket reply via Connection.send: op_list/op_status return names/approval/max_session/description/pid/uid only (no values, no fingerprints); op_preset_validate returns sorted preset NAMES; op_preset_propose pending reply adds only preset NAMES; op_session_start pending reply adds only excluded_per_run (var NAMES); op_import pending reply carries nothing beyond {ok,request_id,pending,notify}. request.summary (which for import holds the CLIENT's own 'sent' secrets + fingerprints of the CLIENT's own values, and for preset holds diff/merged of presets.yaml which contains NO secret values, only var->secretNAME maps) is sent to the client ONLY via request.result after outcome=='approved' (never, no approver). presets.yaml/config.yaml never contain secret values, so even a leaked diff carries none.

IMPORT VALUE-EQUALITY ORACLE is not exposed (re-verified live, deeper than w1). import_resolution() does read every vault value into stored_by_value and WOULD classify a submitted value matching CAPTURE_THE_FLAG's value as 'reused' under its stored name, but that resolution lands only in request.summary (console) and in request.result (approval-only). Live T7: importing CAPTURE_THE_FLAG with a wrong value (7a), a brand-new name+value (7b), and GITHUB_TOKEN with a wrong value (7c) ALL return byte-identical pending replies modulo request_id -> no reply-content differential. No ERROR differential either: renamed_presets rewrites a preset's secret reference to final_names[name], so a referenced import name resolves to either its reused vault name (in known set) or its to_store name (added to the known set) -- parse_presets validation succeeds in BOTH value-match and no-match cases, so no ConfigError oracle. (A string-== in import_resolution on CAPTURE_THE_FLAG's value is not constant-time, but it affects only the approval-gated resolution, is nanoseconds under seconds of yaml/difflib/socket noise, and the value is high-entropy CTF-FLAG-<hex>; not a usable timing oracle. Noted as a hardening nit, not claimed.)

NO UNAPPROVED WRITE (POLICY/PRESET/VAULT INTEGRITY intact). All disk/vault writes (write_presets, vault.set/save, save_presets, save_settings, store_secret, remove_secret, rename_secret) are reachable only inside broker.approve() or the console management flows. Live-confirmed: snapshotted `list`, then fired concurrent op_import (two racing on the same new name RACER with DIFFERENT values valueAAA/valueBBB) + op_preset_propose (mapping Y<-CAPTURE_THE_FLAG) interleaved on three connections, held ~0.8s, dropped. Re-snapshot was BYTE-IDENTICAL to baseline. No preset/secret/session created; the race does not commit anything because nothing commits before approve().

CONCURRENT MULTI-CONNECTION INTERLEAVE cannot leak a reply or apply a change. Each connection is an independent Connection with its own provenance (SO_PEERCRED), one op per connection; there is no shared mutable 'current request' a second connection can hijack. Two connections CAN both attend the same session request (owner's session_wait), but both only await the same never-approved decision future; whichever resolves (only 'withdrawn' is possible) yields an error reply, not a value. request ids are sequential ints but reattach/status/wait are all uid-filtered, so no cross-user id reaches anything.

FORGED / EMPTY / GUESSED SESSION gives nothing. op_run session='' takes the session-LESS path (falsy) -> request_run -> pending (no env). session='deadbeefdeadbeef' -> clean 'unknown session deadbeefdeadbeef'. No CTF-FLAG bytes. (token_hex(8)=64-bit CSPRNG, never leaked to non-owners -- re-confirmed consistent with w1-session findings.)

AUDIT never reaches a socket client. core/audit.Audit.event writes to audit.jsonl (0600 envhsvc) and calls a listener (the console activity feed). It is never sent over the control socket. Its fields carry var NAMES/reason/pid/cmdline/added-reused-renamed NAMES -- never secret values -- and are _short()-truncated+printable()-sanitized regardless. Not a leak channel for a socket client.

CONSOLE request_card static review (in-scope per CHARTER 3.7, NEW-logic-bug angle): content()/import_lines()/key_lines() render secret NAMES, descriptions (already in `list`), and fingerprints of the REQUESTER'S OWN submitted values -- never a vault secret's value. The human-facing 'same value already stored as X' line reveals only a name match to the approver who is deciding. All of it runs only when a console is attached and displaying the card (no console here). No socket-client-triggerable path makes it render a vault value. (It does call broker.merged_presets()->repr-via-dump at render time, re-reachable by the w1-preset-1 alias-repr DoS when a console IS attached, but that is the DoS family + needs a console; not a crown-jewel leak.)
out_of_scope_observations: Reading broker memory / /proc of envhsvc / the 0600 files under /var/lib/envh-ctf would trivially reveal the flag, but is OUT OF SCOPE per CHARTER 3.1-3.3 and was NOT attempted. The flag value was never obtained.

The crown-jewel goal (flag exfil / approval forgery / unapproved write) is, on this build, achievable ONLY with a console approval (a human typing the vault passphrase) or by reading broker memory/files as root -- both out of scope. The socket surface, including all combined/race/TOCTOU angles, is confidentiality- and integrity-sound for a non-root client with no approver.
Config.notify is false in this arena (pending replies carry notify:false); not a vulnerability, just noted for other agents reading replies.

My probes left one detached session_start request (id 25) pending; it is bounded to one per-uid slot and is swept after DETACHED_GRACE (10 min). This is the already-recorded w1-session-1 behavior, not a new finding. I did not flood the shared broker (<=3 concurrent connections, sub-second holds).
best_lead_for_future_waves: There is no socket-reachable crown-jewel crack; the approval gate is the hard boundary and it holds. The only remaining real risk classes are (a) the Wave-1 DoS/event-loop/fd family (needs the ISOLATED broker), (b) the CONSOLE's own rendering/decision logic when an approver IS present (request_card alias-repr DoS; whether a crafted reason/cmdline/preset could mislead a human approver -- a social/display concern, not a socket logic bug), and (c) F7 client-side run-marker kills / F12 cross-user, which are other agents' lanes. For pure flag exfil via the broker protocol, the search space is exhausted: no approver, no leak.
